extracted.intended_audience: researchers applying to SFA grants and donors/fundraisers interested in establishing named research funds
extracted.subtask_description: Policy and procedural guidance for establishing named funds and applying to the Sarcoma Foundation of America (SFA) research grant program, including funding requirements, application materials, review/scoring process, timeline, and reporting expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Named fund establishment funding requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: $55,000 is required for a named request for research proposal. Named research grants can be funded by raising $55,000 or by raising $30,000, whereby the SFA will match the remaining amount or combine two fundraising groups to produce one grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributions to the fund can be targeted towards SFA $50,000 grants and allow new or continued research. Donors may raise the full $55,000 or raise $30,000 and rely on SFA matching or combining groups to reach the grant amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant amount and administrative deduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Out of each $50,000 grant awarded, the SFA uses $5,000 to cover administrative expenses and direct costs of initiating a request for proposals (RFP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and donors should be aware that a portion of awarded funds is retained for administrative/RFP initiation costs; the net available for research is reduced accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Donor restrictions on earmarking/use of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not possible for donors to signify how they want their donations spent (e.g., on a genetic test rather than development of a treatment or a specific sarcoma subtype).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Donations to named funds cannot be earmarked for particular tests, treatments, or subtypes; allocation decisions are made by SFA through its selection process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Request for Proposals asks scientists to submit a proposal outlining their research project along with their professional qualifications and a draft budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should clearly describe the research plan, investigator qualifications, and an itemized draft budget to enable peer review and ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant cycle and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for proposals (RFP) are issued on a cyclical basis. Typical cycle: October–November: Initiate RFP; January: Deadline for proposals; February–March: SFA Medical Advisory Board ranks proposals; April/May: Winners selected and awards announced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adequate funds must be in place before initiating an RFP; donors and applicants should anticipate several months between RFP issuance and award; international advertising/wide circulation is used to maximize competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review process and scoring system
rubrics_metrics.description: Each research proposal is reviewed by SFA’s Medical Advisory Board, composed of leading academic sarcoma experts, and ranked through a scoring system. SFA’s grant review process is based on the same peer review system utilized by the National Institutes of Health (NIH). Scoring of grants is done individually by each medical expert and scores are added together to determine the final ranking of each proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews may include both internal and external medical reviewers; highest scoring proposals are recommended for funding to SFA’s Board of Directors. The NIH-style individual scoring and aggregation determine ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest policy for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Any reviewer with a conflict of interest is excused from voting on a specific proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must recuse themselves where conflicts exist to preserve impartiality of the scoring and selection process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for funding decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Selections for funding are based on scores from internal and external medical reviewers, available funding, and the predicted potential for the research effort to result in improved therapeutic options for sarcoma patients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards are based solely on scientific merit, with final recommendations from the Medical Advisory Board and final votes by SFA’s Board of Directors; available funds and potential clinical/therapeutic impact are considered alongside scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring, reporting, and completion expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: After the grant is awarded, SFA monitors the progress of the research, requiring an annual report to SFA’s Medical Advisory Board. A final report is required from investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must submit periodic (annual) progress reports and a final report; project timelines may vary and some projects may require more or less time for completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement of international competition and wide dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: By encouraging research applicants to compete against each other on an international basis, SFA’s Research Grant Program funds only the best proposals that are most likely to result in research breakthroughs applicable to diagnosis or treatment of people with sarcoma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SFA issues broadly circulated RFPs and advises donors that maximizing competition (including international applicants) increases the likelihood that the most meritorious projects are funded; this contributes to longer lead times between RFP issuance and awards.
